question: to the Commission Catherine Griset (PfE) Subject:

The US Supreme Court has paved the way for the President of the United States to dismiss the commissioners of the Federal Trade Commission, the agency responsible, amongst other things, for protecting the personal data of Europeans when it is processed by US tech firms1. Since 1935, the independence of these commissioners had been based on protection against politically-motivated dismissal: the President of the United States could appoint them, but could not remove them from office. The US Supreme Court has now made such removal possible which, in turn, runs counter to the data transfer agreement, concluded by the European Union with the United States, and known as the ‘Data Privacy Framework’. This agreement was in fact conditional upon the existence of independent supervisory authorities in the United States. Does the Commission plan to renegotiate the data transfer agreement with the United States, given that the legal challenges already brought before the Court of Justice of the European Union have a strong chance of success?
